# Documentation tooling

`docs/index.html` ("Mosaic — Documentation Hub") is a hand-built single-page
markdown browser: a sidebar `<a onclick="loadFile(...)">` link per doc, grouped
under `<h3>` headers, rendered client-side via marked.js. Serve it over
`http://` (e.g. `python3 -m http.server` from `docs/`) — `fetch()` of local
files is blocked under `file://` in most browsers.

## Auto-generated vs. hand-curated groups

Two groups stay fully hand-maintained: `General` and `Project & Legal`. Both
mix root-level files (`README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`) with hand-picked docs and
custom labels — low-churn, edited rarely, genuinely want human judgment about
what belongs and how it's titled. Nothing in this repo regenerates them.

The other 8 groups map 1:1 to a `docs/` subdirectory and are regenerated by
`tools/docs/regenerate_nav.py`:

| Group               | Directory                | Sort order    |
|---------------------|---------------------------|---------------|
| Record               | `docs/record/`             | newest first  |
| Updates & Summaries  | `docs/updates/`            | newest first  |
| Architecture         | `docs/architecture/`       | alphabetical  |
| Design               | `docs/design/`             | alphabetical  |
| Reference            | `docs/reference/`          | alphabetical  |
| RFCs                 | `docs/rfcs/`               | alphabetical  |
| Design Specs         | `docs/superpowers/specs/`  | oldest first  |
| Implementation Plans | `docs/superpowers/plans/`  | oldest first  |

Each group's link list in `docs/index.html` is wrapped in
`<!-- AUTO-GENERATED:key --> ... <!-- END-AUTO-GENERATED -->` markers; the
`<h3>` label itself is never touched by the script (renaming a group is a
deliberate manual edit). Adding a new file to one of the 7 mapped directories
is now enough on its own — no `index.html` edit required — as long as someone
reruns the generator afterward (see below).

## Running it

```bash
python3 tools/docs/regenerate_nav.py
```
Overwrites `docs/index.html` in place, regenerating only the 7 auto-groups.
Safe to run any time — idempotent (running it twice with no doc changes
produces a byte-identical file), and it never touches `General`/
`Project & Legal`. Runs automatically via `.githooks/pre-commit`
(`git config core.hooksPath .githooks` opts a clone in), which blocks a
commit if regenerating changes anything — still safe to run by hand at
any other time, e.g. to preview a change before committing.

## Title derivation

Each file's title comes from its own first `# ` heading (backticks stripped,
nothing else shortened) — most files in this repo already follow that
convention, so most titles come through verbatim. A file with no `# `-prefixed
first line falls back to a filename-derived title (strips a date prefix and a
`-design`/`-plan` suffix, title-cases the rest) and the generator prints a
warning naming it, since a missing heading is worth a human's attention.

**Accepted trade-off:** this project's oldest specs/plans predate a settled
"clean one-line title" convention, so a few of their auto-derived titles are
more verbose than the hand-picked labels the nav used to show for them (e.g.
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-15-mosaic-docs-hub.md`'s real first line is
`# Project Mosaic — Documentation Set & Docs Hub Implementation Plan`, longer
than the old hand-shortened "Docs Hub Setup"). This is the accepted cost of
full automation — a manual title-override system would reintroduce the same
staleness risk this tool exists to remove.

**A permanent case of this fallback:** `docs/reference/components.md`
(generated by `mosaic docs`, see below) opens with an HTML-comment
auto-generated banner rather than a `# ` heading as its literal first line —
title derivation only checks the first non-blank line, so it never reaches
the `# Component Reference` heading a few lines further down, and the nav
shows the filename-derived "Components" instead. Every rerun of the
generator prints the fallback warning for this file; this is expected, not
a regression, and not worth chasing (regenerating `components.md` never
changes its first line, since `mosaic docs` always emits that same banner).

## Component reference docs (`mosaic docs`)

A CLI subcommand, `mosaic docs`, walks every built-in engine component via
`ComponentReflection` and generates `docs/reference/components.md` — one
combined markdown page listing every component's fields and their default
values. `docs/reference/` is the 7th auto-generated nav group above.
`FieldVisitor::field_readonly` is still used uniformly for `bool` and
non-`float` numeric types, so the generated page can show a field's name and
default value but not a precise type label for those — documented in the
generated page's own intro. `EntityID` and `Handle<R>` fields are no longer
part of that limitation: `MarkdownFieldVisitor` overrides `field_entity`/
`field_handle_asset` and renders them with an explicit `(entity)`/`(asset via
Handle)` suffix instead. `mosaic docs` also generates
`docs/reference/scripting-globals.md` from pybind11 docstring annotations on
the `install_world_globals`/`imgui_*` registrations. Full design (component
reference): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-component-reference-docs-design.md`.
Full design (scripting-globals reference):
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-16-scripting-globals-reference-docs-design.md`.

Full design (nav generator): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-docs-hub-nav-generator-design.md`.
